surfaces.part: top board of the bookshelf (plank rows)
shelf compartments with books, seen face-on, and the thin shelf boards

answer.evidence: Rows 1-6 are a wood-plank band. The band ends in a lighter front-edge line at row 6 (L=195), followed by a dark eave row at row 7 (L=103), so it reads as a top surface about 6 rows tall. Below it, rows 7-30 (about 24 rows) are the vertical front face: three shelf bays with books, divided by a central post. The silhouette is a constant 30 px wide with no side face. The object is a bookshelf, which only loosely fits the 'large structure' kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small wooden bookshelf with coloured book spines, about 30x27 source pixels. It has no roof, no door or window, and no wall and roof material ramps, so it does not read as a whole building next to the two references. The measured facts do not count against it: 22 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, which means the outline is tinted. The outline is dark brown beside the wood. The wood frame itself has only about 4 shading steps (light edge, mid, dark, outline), and the shelf interior is mostly book-colour dots. The references show 5-6 steps on roof tiles plus plaster and stone texture. Since the piece is not a building, there is no roof ramp to compare, and the comparison cannot confirm Beodeul-level building craft. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: top plank surface of the shelf unit

answer.evidence: This is a front-facing bookshelf and fills the tile. Rows 1-5 are a light plank-textured band across the full width, like the top of the green reference cabinet. Row 6 (L=195) is a lighter front-edge line, and row 7 (L=103) is a dark eave shadow. Below that, rows 7-30 form a 24-row front face with the bay frame, shelf boards at rows 13-14, 21-22 and 29, and books visible in each bay. The top band is more than a 1-2 row rim. The kind 'structure (gate, pavilion, building)' fits poorly, since this reads as furniture (a shelf), though the drawing is large.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny bookshelf-like prop, about one tile in size. It has a wood frame and rows of coloured books, but no roof, no walls and no door. It does not read as a whole building, so it can't be compared fairly with the tiled-roof, timber and stone houses. The measured facts are fine on paper: 22 visible tones per tile against 10-12 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edges. That fits the tinted dark-brown outline I can see around the wood. By eye, though, the frame carries only about 3 wood steps, against 5-6 on the reference roofs and walls. There are no tile scallops, plaster speckle or stone shading. The book rows add colour variety but little graded shading. As a building it falls well short of the Beodeul standard, so it fails.
